Subject: Questions on 'anchoring' & eviction for Private VPC deployment

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team has a few follow-ups specific to the Private/VPC offering. They used the term 'anchoring' to describe a capability we'd like: the ability for Everwell to create cryptographic time-stamped artifacts that prove a data snapshot existed at X time and where it was stored, and then later request an "eviction" (full wipe and certificate).

Can Redwood outline:
- Whether we can get signed snapshots or manifests (hash lists) that we control/retain.
- What evidence you can provide after an eviction: certificate of deletion, chain-of-custody logs, and any live playback of deletion operations (timestamps, operator id).
- How encryption keys factor in (do we hold KMS keys, use BYOK, or a joint model?).
- Expected timelines between a tenant eviction request and final irrevocable wipe across mirrors/backups (and any retention tombstone windows).

I've attached our question spreadsheet. Can you loop in the engineering folks? We're evaluating this for compliance with our data residency and retention policy.

Elena

Elena — thanks for the detailed sheet and the clear framing. Quick summary up-front: yes — Redwood Private can support cryptographic anchors and a verifiable eviction workflow; below are the high-level options and then Karthik and Monica will provide technical details and timelines.

High-level options we propose:
1) Customer-controlled anchor artifacts: We can generate a signed manifest (SHA256 hashes + object paths + timestamp) that we sign with Redwood's platform signing key and also optionally store a customer-provided HMAC key so you can verify integrity. You keep the manifest externally.

2) BYOK + sealed-erase: For strongest assurances, customers can hold KMS keys (BYOK) for tenant encryption. After an eviction request, Redwood executes a sealed-erase (cryptographic key destruction) and provides a signed deletion token.

3) Proof-of-eviction pack: Post-eviction we can emit a package containing deletion logs, operator audit trail, snapshot manifests, and a signed statement of completion. We can additionally provide an independent hash of the package that you keep as a record.

Open items we will confirm: snapshot retention windows, cross-region mirror wipe timelines, and any archival snapshot reconciliation windows. Karthik — can you confirm our current timelines (SLA-ish) for the Private deployment path and what logs we can include in the pack? Monica — can you add any commercialization/contract notes (e.g., additional work for BYOK onboarding)?

Next step: I'd like to schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through this week. Proposed slots: Thu 8/30 10:00-10:30 PDT or Fri 8/31 11:00-11:30 PDT. Which works?

Best,
Dylan

Elena / team — thanks for the questions. I'm on the engineering side for Private deployments; below are concrete answers and caveats so you can present them to your compliance folks.

1) Signed snapshot manifests (anchoring) - We can create manifest files containing per-object SHA256, object path, size, and a UTC timestamp. Manifests are signed with a Redwood platform signing key (ECDSA-256) and can also include an HMAC computed with a customer-supplied secret for your independent verification. We can export manifests on-demand or as scheduled snapshots (daily/hourly depending on config).

2) Eviction workflow & evidence - Trigger: eviction requests must be sent via the Redwood Console (Admin action) and are recorded as an auditable event. Workflows:
  - Standard eviction: initiate wipe across primary storage and authoritative replicas; final step is a tombstone marking with a 72-hour reconciliation window to allow in-flight writes to quiesce.
  - Forensic/accelerated eviction: when required, we can perform accelerated wipes and escalate to manual verification; this incurs an operational runbook activation and SLA depends on region and workload.

Evidence we provide after completion:
  - Signed deletion certificate (includes tenant id, timestamp, operator id, and manifest hash)
  - Low-level audit logs covering API calls and internal operator actions (redacted as needed)
  - Snapshot of pre-eviction manifest and post-eviction manifest (post-eviction manifest will be an empty manifest confirming object absence)
  - Optional notarization: for regulated customers we can route the deletion certificate to a third-party auditor for attestation (contract work).

3) Backups & replication - Important caveat: snapshots that are exported (e.g., to a customer-controlled S3) remain in your control and are not deleted by Redwood unless requested. For Redwood-managed replicas and cross-region copies, our typical reconciliation window is up to 7 days in edge-cases, but normal completion is 72 hours. If you require cryptographic key destruction (BYOK), destruction of your KMS key renders data unreadable immediately subject to provider KMS policies.

4) Keys & BYOK - BYOK is strongly recommended for the highest assurance. We support AWS KMS external key material and customer-managed keys for Private installs. If you hold the key, physical deletion/destruction of key material is the fastest way to achieve effective irrevocability. We can provide guidance on key lifecycle.

5) For legal hold and discovery - If Everwell places a legal hold, eviction is delayed until release. We can provide a manifest and continued isolation to satisfy discovery requests.

6) Operational proofs & replay - We can provide a machine-readable "proof pack" (JSON + zipped logs + signed manifests) that your security team can ingest. We will redact internal PII as needed.

Timeline summary (typical):
  - Standard eviction (primary+replicas): 72 hours to completion + issuance of deletion certificate
  - Accelerated/forensic eviction: variable; expect 1–5 business days depending on manual steps and notarization
  - BYOK cryptographic destruction: immediate upon key destruction but subject to KMS provider propagation (typically under 24 hours)

Limitations & next steps:
  - We cannot delete external customer exports (objects you pulled into your own S3) — those remain your responsibility.
  - If you need notarized deletion certificates, that requires an engagement and schedule we can provide in an SOW.

Dylan — happy to join the call. Elena — I'll bring a short runbook and an example proof pack. Monica — please flag any commercial impacts (BYOK onboarding fee / notarization cost).

Thanks,
Karthik
